scope: Experimental precise mesh screen-selection index, worker transport and shared scan_select_region operation; no rendered browser session was exercised.
problem: Number-array mesh positions were rounded to world-space Float32 both in the worker client and BVH, collapsing a small triangle at X=100000000.
change: Mesh number-array inputs are transferred to workers as Float64Array; the selection BVH uses Float32 coordinates relative to the mesh bounds center. Ray origins and broad-phase bounds are translated between local BVH and world coordinates; clipping remains world-space. Worker-count estimation accounts for the larger precise input. Float32 mesh and point-cloud transport retain their prior representation.
coverage: Controls compare rectangle, brush, through, clipping, visibility and partition masks; the scan_select_region operation calls the same index in a mocked host and produces the same mask as the direct selection control. The actual worker dispatcher was invoked in-process with structured-cloned output. Neither test is an actual browser worker, rendered GUI or public MCP transport.

validation.tests: 26 tests across screen selection, worker client, in-process worker dispatcher and public operation: m2-selection-precision-budget-green-20261028-r2-guard.json.
validation.typecheck: Focused TypeScript passed with Node and Vite types under m2-selection-precision-types-20261028-r3-guard.json. The first ad hoc typecheck omitted Node types and failed in unrelated timer declarations; it was not a source-code failure.
validation.large: A manufactured 400000-triangle number-array mesh retained the selected triangle and source values under m2-selection-large-precision-20261028-r2-guard.json; peak job bytes 373579776. This is an in-process test, not browser-worker memory measurement.

limitations: The BVH remains Float32, so local precision depends on mesh spatial extent.
Viewport rendering and other picking paths still require local-origin assessment; this change does not prove rendered precision.
The finite Split candidate is not connected to production, and native parity and actual GUI/public MCP validation remain open.
